name: apprenti.dev Engineering Foundations for Junior Developers
audience: New graduates or junior developers in their first months in a professional engineering role, who can already write code but have little professional practice
philosophy: LEARN BY DOING. GROW THROUGH MENTORSHIP. The professional practices a degree or bootcamp usually skips: real Git workflows, reading unfamiliar code, testing what already exists, methodical debugging, and writing for a reviewer.
assumptions: Weekly hours (10-15) assume this curriculum runs alongside a structured onboarding program, where task work is one part of the week rather than the whole of it; a fully self-paced apprentice may need a different pace.
Apprentices already know how to program in at least one language before starting. This curriculum teaches professional practice, not language fundamentals.
Python is used as the shared implementation language for hands-on tasks so evidence is comparable across apprentices; Git, tooling, and review tasks are otherwise kept language-agnostic.
aiPrinciples: AI assistance must be disclosed when materially used.
Tasks in this curriculum default to guided AI use: explanations, hints and quizzes are allowed, complete solutions are not.
The apprentice remains accountable for every submitted artifact, AI-assisted or not.
Mentor approval is based on demonstrated understanding and inspectable evidence, not on AI output quality.
